name: Ather Energy Ltd
title: Ather Energy Ltd - 544397 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Demand far exceeds supply: wholesale up 81% to 83,000 units, dealer inventory cut to 3 days, and capacity expansion (AURIC, 4.2 to 9.2 lakh units) is the key supply response, while commodity costs cut gross margin to 22.4%.

summary.headline: Ather Energy Q1 FY27: wholesale volumes up 81% to 83,000 units, first-ever positive EBITDA of Rs 9 crore (~0.8% margin), AGM down to 22.4%.
summary.overview: Management described a sharp demand upswing driven by policy support, fuel-availability concerns and TCO gains, with registrations up 102% YoY and paid preorders up 158% to 1.5 lakh. Production was constrained at the Hosur plant (35,000 units/month max, reached near full utilisation by June), leaving dealer inventory at about 3 days versus 14 days earlier. Commodity costs rose sharply, cutting adjusted gross margin by 5.6 percentage points to 22.4%, partly offset by an average selling price rise to Rs 1.61 lakh and disciplined fixed-cost control that delivered the first positive EBITDA. Management expects further commodity hits of 100-200 bps, to be largely offset by price increases that were only partly reflected in Q1.

segments.name: Middle India (Gujarat, Maharashtra, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 141% YoY, the highest of all zones in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Rest of India
segments.commentary: Retail grew 118% YoY in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: South India
segments.commentary: Retail grew 76% YoY in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Non-vehicle revenue (AtherStack Pro, accessories, services)
segments.commentary: AtherStack Pro is the largest non-vehicle item; service revenue is about 2-3% of revenue versus 10-12% for established two-wheeler peers; accessories undisclosed.

guidance_outlook: Commodity headwind: management expects a further 100-200 bps hit beyond the 5.6% in Q1, to be largely absorbed through price hikes; Q2 full-quarter ASP benefit expected.

AURIC Phase 1 (Aurangabad, Factory 3.0) go-live later in calendar 2026; expected to take total capacity from 4.2 lakh to 9.2 lakh units per year; full ramp to 42,000 units/month in 4-5 months, possibly spilling into early FY28.
EL scooter (brand name to be unveiled) launch later in August 2026; target 60,000 units/month capacity across Aurangabad and Hosur (42,000 from AURIC Phase 1 plus 18,000 from Hosur).
AURIC Phase 2 could add 5 lakh units/year (total 14.2 lakh); planning stage only, firmer timeline possibly within a quarter or two.
Fundraise: Rs 1,300 crore QIP completed; a further Rs 1,200 crore preference issue pending shareholder approval, total Rs 2,500 crore.
PM E-DRIVE subsidy extension awaited; about 15-20% of Q1 vehicles sold without subsidy; Q2 subsidy treatment uncertain.
capex_capacity: Hosur plant: maximum 35,000 units/month (about 4.2 lakh/year), near 100% utilisation as of the call; can allocate 18,000 units/month to EL or to Rizta/450X, not both.

AURIC (Aurangabad) Phase 1: equipment installation ending in next couple of months; trial production from festive period; reliable daily output from 1 January; assembly line set up, paint shop under trial.
Ather Community Day on 29 August 2026 in Bengaluru to unveil the EL scooter.
New store openings slowed in Q1; expected to surge once EL and AURIC are live around the festive season. Stores reportedly reach operational profitability in about 5-6 months on average.
demand_pricing: Industry e-2W penetration reported at 11%, up 44%; industry registrations up 68% YoY to 525k in Q1 FY27; Ather inquiries up 95%; over 7 lakh inquiries in Q1; Ather brand searches up about 118%.

Management estimates unrealised retail potential of 13,000-15,000 units per month above the roughly 30,000 units/month retailed; some dealers have stopped accepting preorders with waits of about 2 months.
Pricing power: ASP moved from Rs 1.5 lakh (Q4) to Rs 1.53 lakh (April and May) and Rs 1.61 lakh (June), with price hikes described as 100% margin accretive.
Customer profile reportedly unchanged; retail finance and TCO advantage cited as supporting willingness to pay higher prices.
EL launch expected to depress ASP somewhat, with launch focus on northern and rest-of-India markets and attach rate guided at least 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the commodity headwind be a similar 5-6% again next quarter, or stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a further 100-200 bps of hit, not 5-6%, and says commodity costs may be near the top; quarterly averages understate end-of-quarter costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 employee and other expense control a new baseline before AURIC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not exceptional, reflecting cautious spending in FY27 after a strong FY26; some AURIC costs will be capitalised initially, with P&L impact from Q4 onwards alongside volume.

qa_highlights.question: How does 60,000 EL capacity relate to Hosur's 35,000 capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: AURIC Phase 1 is dedicated to EL at 42,000/month; Hosur gives flexibility of 18,000 units/month, shared with Rizta and 450X, so total is 60,000 for EL and not additive.

qa_highlights.question: Can AURIC Phase 2 be brought forward, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 is in planning; the Rs 2,500 crore raise gives funding to fast-track it, with firmer timelines possibly within one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for non-vehicle revenue and service?
qa_highlights.answer: AtherStack Pro is the largest non-vehicle item and benefited from price increases; service revenue is about 2-3% of revenue versus 10-12% for mature peers, and is expected to compound with fleet size.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ather enter electric motorcycles soon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is focused on EL platform products over the next year; a motorcycle launch is more than a year away, probably two years or more.

risks_watch: Commodity costs could rise a further 100-200 bps; margin recovery depends on price increases and commodity cooling, which management says is hard to predict.
PM E-DRIVE subsidy extension not yet confirmed; about 15-20% of Q1 volumes sold without subsidy.
AURIC Phase 1 ramp risk: go-live slated for later in 2026, possible slip into early FY28; supply already short of demand by about 15,000 units per month per analyst.
EL launch may lower ASP and could cannibalise Rizta; attach-rate and margin mix to be watched.
Dealer inventory at about 3 days leaves little buffer; new store additions paused until capacity arrives.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and pricing power, with management calling demand unprecedented and the first positive EBITDA a milestone. More cautious on commodity costs and timelines, repeatedly declining to commit to exact AURIC ramp months or Phase 2 dates.
key_quotes: Happy to report that our teams have been able to drive very strong success on both added sales price increase and improved SKU.
Our EBITDA came in at a Rs. 9 crore margin for Q1 2027, which is roughly about 0.8%.
Hosur can anyways do 35,000 a month, and we are also trying to push that up a little bit more.
I would cautiously guide at least 75% attach rates with EL also, but I would hope for even higher.
